correctness.rationale: The exact length-two geodesic obstruction is equivalent to a selected bipartite edge with both endpoint degrees at least two. This yields the star-forest characterization. A legal-single-edge extension analysis proves an exhaustive three-way maximality partition; exponential labeled-component counting and independent finite sum give the polynomial. Spanning forests have between 2 and m components for m<=n; explicit two-star-plus-singleton constructions attain each permitted component count. Brute graph-distance tests on all 1,152,848 subsets of nine small instances independently match every coefficient. Finite checks are not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a complete, natural enumerative invariant on every rectangular rook graph, connecting maximal geodesic-free configurations to spanning star forests and quantifying an arbitrarily long cardinality gap. The exact number of maximal sets at each length is not a routine consequence of the already known minimum and maximum. Both the spectrum and its multiplicities can inform general-position achievement/avoidance move-length analysis without making an unproved strategy claim.
